newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: UNDP SAYS S.AFRICAN STANDARD OF LIVING IMPROVES.
newsitem.headline: UNDP SAYS S.AFRICAN STANDARD OF LIVING IMPROVES.

text.p: The U.N. Development Programme (UNDP) said in a report released on Thursday that South Africa had in the last year moved up 10 places in a global ranking based on a "human development index".
"The political momentum of the struggle against apartheid is now driving the struggle against human poverty," the annual report said.
"However, progress has been uneven and stark disparities exist between different race groups," it added.
The report said in terms of human development South Africa now ranked 90th in the world, ccompared with 100th in 1996.
"The human development index is a composite of measurements based on whether people live a long and healthy life, are educated and enjoy a decent standard of living," the report said.
"South Africa improved its score due mainly to revisions of the data for life expectancy and real GDP per capita."
South Africa had the best figures of countries in continental sub-Saharan African, although it was behind Seychelles and Mauritius.
Canada is at the top of the global ranking.
